extracted.intended_audience: registered practitioners and patent agents who practice before the USPTO (and their firms), USPTO OED staff, and others interested in practitioner disciplinary rules
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and disciplinary criteria governing the conduct of persons who practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office, with specific citations to pre- and post‑May 3, 2013 rules and examples of conduct that violates those rules. Includes required sanctions/conditions for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.65 — business transaction with client (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to May 3, 2013, a practitioner must not enter into a business transaction with a client without the client's consent after full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each time a client signed a Research Engagement Letter and a Professional Services Contract with MIPA/SAI/FSBI (to which Respondent had an ownership interest), Respondent failed to obtain client consent after full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.108(a) — business transaction with client (post-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: On or after May 3, 2013, a practitioner must not enter into a business transaction with a client without obtaining informed consent in writing signed by the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PSC and Research Engagement Letter were entered into without written informed consent acknowledging Respondent's ownership interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.68(a)(1) — accepting compensation from non-client (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to May 3, 2013, a practitioner must not accept compensation from someone other than the client for the practitioner's services without obtaining consent after full disclosure from the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent accepted payments from MIPA for patent law services rendered to clients referred by MIPA without client consent after full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.108(f) — accepting compensation from non-client (post-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: On or after May 3, 2013, practitioner may not accept compensation from one other than the client for representing the client unless conditions (informed consent, independence of professional judgment, confidentiality protection) are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent accepted compensation from MIPA for work on referred clients without obtaining informed consent and without ensuring independence/confidentiality safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.102(c) — unbundling/limiting scope of services
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may limit the scope of representation only if the limitation is reasonable and the client gives informed consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility packages sold by MIPA limited prosecution services (e.g., no Office Action responses) without practitioner consultation or obtaining informed consent from clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.105(b) — communicate scope and basis of fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of representation and the basis or rate of the fee and expenses for which the client will be responsible shall be communicated to the client, preferably in writing, before or within a reasonable time after commencing representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSC changes that reduced prosecution coverage were not explained to clients by a registered practitioner prior to purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.62(a) and § 10.66(a) — conflicts affecting independent professional judgment (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to May 3, 2013, a practitioner must not accept or continue employment when the practitioner's independent professional judgment will be or is likely to be adversely affected by the practitioner's financial, business, or personal interests (and must decline employment in such circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's ownership and financial ties to MIPA/SAI/FSBI created conflicts affecting judgment when representing referred clients without consent after full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.107(a)(2) — concurrent conflicts of interest (post-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: On or after May 3, 2013, a practitioner must not represent a client where a concurrent conflict of interest exists unless the client gives informed consent, confirmed in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent failed to obtain clients' informed consent to representation despite personal and financial connections with the referring companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2) — reasonable consultation about means
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must reasonably consult with the client about the means by which the client's objectives are to be accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent adhered to a business practice of not consulting with clients about the specific type of patent application and instead prepared the type sold by non-practitioner salespersons.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(b) — explain matters sufficiently for informed decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must explain a matter to the extent reasonably necessary to permit the client to make informed decisions regarding the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent and MP&D did not explain the likelihood of obtaining a patent of 'useful scope' or the consequences of the chosen application type, so clients could not make informed decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.68(b) — third party direction of practitioner's judgment (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to May 3, 2013, a practitioner must not permit a person who recommends, employs, or pays the practitioner to direct or regulate the practitioner's professional judgment in rendering such services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent permitted MIPA/SAI/FSBI influence (salesperson-determined application types) over the professional judgment used in preparing and filing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.201 — exercise independent professional judgment and candid advice
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must exercise independent professional judgment and render candid advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent failed to exercise independent judgment by adhering to sales-driven practices and filing application types sold by non-practitioner salespersons instead of advising clients based on professional analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.504(c) — third party directing practitioner's judgment (post-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a person who recommends, employs, or pays the practitioner to render legal services for another from directing or regulating the practitioner's professional judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same factual pattern: allowing MIPA/SAI/FSBI to dictate the type of patent filing to be prepared and filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.47(a) — aiding non-practitioner in unauthorized practice (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must not aid non-practitioners in the unauthorized practice of law before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent provided template recommendation letters to non‑practitioner salespersons, knowing they would be used to consult with inventors and sell patent services without practitioner consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) — conduct prejudicial to administration of justice (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must not engage in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice, including aiding unauthorized practice of law by non‑practitioner salespersons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing letters and materially assisting salespersons who sold patent services to unsophisticated clients without practitioner contact was considered prejudicial conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.505 — assisting others to practice in violation of jurisdictional rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits assisting another in practicing law in a jurisdiction in violation of that jurisdiction's regulation of the legal profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's actions in enabling non-practitioner salespersons to provide legal advice about patent application types could amount to assisting unauthorized practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) — conduct prejudicial to administration of justice (post-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to pre-2013 provision; use of template letters to enable non-practitioner advice and sales was prejudicial.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) — disreputable or gross misconduct (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct (e.g., providing misleading template documents rather than true opinions to unsophisticated clients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent provided template 'opinions' that did not describe the likelihood of obtaining a patent of useful scope despite representations on the referral company's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.57(b)(1) — revealing client confidences without consent (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits revealing a confidence or secret of a client without consent after full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referring work to outside registered practitioners without clients' consent to share confidential client information violated this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.106(a) — confidentiality of client information (post-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits revealing information relating to the representation of a client without the client's informed consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent revealed clients' invention information to outside practitioners without informed consent when referring work.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.37(a) — dividing fees with non-firm practitioners (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to May 3, 2013, a practitioner must not divide a fee for legal services with another practitioner who is not a partner or associate in the practitioner's firm without client consent after full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent shared fees with outside registered practitioners to whom he referred work without obtaining clients' consent after full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.105(e) — dividing fees between practitioners not in same firm (post-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee may be divided between practitioners who are not in the same firm only if (1) division is proportionate to services or they assume joint responsibility, (2) client agrees to arrangement including share each will receive and agreement is in writing, and (3) total fee is reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent failed to satisfy these conditions when sharing fees with outside practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112 — safekeeping property (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires depositing advance fees for patent law services (other than advance costs and expenses such as USPTO fees) into a client trust account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MIPA/SAI/FSBI and Respondent did not deposit unearned legal fees paid in advance into a client trust account.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115 — safekeeping property (post-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires depositing advanced fees for patent law services (and for other advanced costs and expenses such as USPTO fees) into a client trust account and maintaining required records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent did not maintain a client trust account and failed to deposit unearned fees into a trust; as a reinstatement/probation condition he must submit trust account records every six months under § 11.115(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.48 — sharing fees with non-practitioner (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits sharing fees with a non-practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent shared fees with MIPA/SAI/FSBI by virtue of his permanent and ongoing business relationship with those non-practitioner entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.49 — forming partnership with non-practitioner (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits forming a partnership with a non-practitioner if any of the partnership activities consist of the practice of law before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's business relationship and his father's ownership interest in MP&D raised issues under this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.504(a) — sharing legal fees with non-practitioner (post-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a practitioner from sharing legal fees with a non-practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's ongoing business relationship with MIPA/SAI/FSBI resulted in fee-sharing with non-practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.504(d)(1) — forming a practice with non-practitioner ownership (post-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits practicing in a professional association or corporation authorized to practice for a profit if a non-practitioner owns any interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's firm structure and non-practitioner ownership (his father) implicated this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.504(d)(1) — practicing in association with non-practitioner (alternate phrasing)
rubrics_metrics.description: On or after May 3, 2013, practitioners must not practice in a for-profit association with non-practitioner ownership that affects the practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated finding that non-practitioner ownership in MP&D (during the relevant time) violated this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and disclosures about firm/referral relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must disclose ownership, financial interests, and familial ties that could create conflicts and must obtain informed consent when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent failed to disclose ownership and financial ties to MIPA/SAI/FSBI and did not disclose that 90% of MP&D’s income came from referrals from those entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for opinions of patentability and competence in client communications
rubrics_metrics.description: When representing or providing legal opinions, practitioners must provide meaningful advice (e.g., discussing likelihood of obtaining a patent of useful scope) consistent with representations made to clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's template 'opinions' merely suggested an application type and did not explain likelihood of obtaining a patent of useful scope despite website representations promising an opinion of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on non-practitioner salespersons giving legal advice or selling legal services
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-practitioner salespersons must not engage in unauthorized practice of law or provide legal advice about patent strategy in lieu of practitioner consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MIPA non-practitioner commissioned salespersons consulted with inventors and sold patent application packages without registered practitioner consultation; Respondent facilitated this by providing template recommendations for use by salespersons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension from practice before USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be suspended from practice before the Office in patent matters for forty-eight (48) months commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the agreed disciplinary sanction resolving the stipulated misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction condition: eligibility and timing for petition for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be eligible to file a petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(b) twenty-one (21) months after the Final Order; no petition shall be granted prior to 24 months after the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED Director will proceed with review; reinstatement subject to compliance with other listed conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction condition: MPRE requirement for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of reinstatement, Respondent must take the Multi-State Professional Responsibility Examination (MPRE) and attain a score of 85 or better, and provide a declaration with corroborating documents verifying compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must pay for and pass the MPRE with score >=85 before reinstatement is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction condition: audit a legal ethics class for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of reinstatement, Respondent shall audit a legal ethics class at an ABA-accredited law school and provide a declaration with corroborating documents verifying compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must complete this at his own expense prior to reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation reporting requirements after reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon reinstatement, Respondent shall serve a 24‑month probationary period and, every six months during probation, submit records required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(f) and certify that his and MP&D's client trust account(s) are in full compliance with the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply may trigger an Order to Show Cause and additional suspension up to 24 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and § 11.59 (conditions and OED procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (conditions on reinstatement) and the OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 (procedures for petitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of reinstatement procedures Respondent must submit a supplemental affidavit attesting compliance with § 11.58 no sooner than 23 months and 3 weeks after the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and publication obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall publish the Final Order in OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a materially consistent notice in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice summarizes suspension, reinstatement conditions, and factual background for public notice and practitioner guidance.
